cards.b: A diagram showing a business's internal structure: levels of hierarchy, departments and who reports to whom.
The number of subordinates working directly under a manager.
The route through which instructions pass down from senior management to lower levels.
Flat: few levels, wide spans, faster communication, more delegation. Tall: many levels, narrow spans, close supervision, slow communication.
Giving a subordinate the authority to perform particular tasks. The manager is still responsible for the result.
Manager decides alone with one-way communication. Suits emergencies, quick decisions and unskilled or new staff.
Democratic: workers involved in decisions, two-way communication. Laissez-faire: broad objectives, workers decide, little direction.
A group of workers who join together to protect their interests (pay, conditions, job security) through collective bargaining.
Job description: duties and responsibilities of the job. Person specification: qualifications, skills and qualities needed in the person.
Internal: existing employee; cheaper, quicker, motivating but narrow choice. External: wider choice and new ideas but costlier and slower.
Introduction for a new employee to the business: layout, policies, health and safety, colleagues.
On-the-job: at the workplace with an experienced worker; cheap but bad habits. Off-the-job: away from work; wider skills but costly and work time lost.
Dismissal: sacked for poor work or behaviour. Redundancy: job no longer needed; not the worker's fault.
Sender, message, medium, receiver, then feedback. Two-way communication includes feedback.
Jargon, long or unclear message, wrong medium, long chain of command, no feedback, noise or technology failure.

gaps.s: The levels of management in a business from highest to lowest are called the ___ .
A wide span of control usually means a ___ organisation structure.
A job ___ lists the duties and responsibilities of a job.
A worker who loses their job because they are no longer needed has been made ___ .
Training that introduces a new employee to the business is called ___ training.
Giving a subordinate authority to do tasks is called ___ .
A manager who makes all decisions alone has an ___ leadership style.
Email and intranet are examples of ___ communication.

short.q: State two benefits of a flat organisation structure. [2]
short.model: Faster communication and fewer managers (lower costs); more delegation motivates workers.

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of recruiting externally. [4]
short.model: Advantage: wider choice of candidates and new ideas. Disadvantage: more expensive (advertising) and slower, with a longer induction.

short.q: Explain the difference between dismissal and redundancy. [3]
short.model: Dismissal is when a worker is sacked for unsatisfactory work or behaviour. Redundancy is when the job is no longer needed, not due to the worker's performance.

short.q: Explain why a democratic leadership style may suit a team of experienced designers. [3]
short.model: Skilled designers have ideas worth hearing. Involving them in decisions raises motivation and commitment through two-way communication.

short.q: Explain two problems of a long chain of command for communication. [4]
short.model: Messages pass through many levels, so they are slow. They can also be distorted, which means workers misunderstand instructions.
